applied.quote: Your report changes as balances post, accounts open, and payments arrive, so a score pulled at the start of a month can differ from one pulled weeks later.
applied.replacement: A score can differ depending on the day it was calculated.

applied.quote: A side-by-side look at the two main credit scoring models and why the score on a free app may not match the one a lender pulls.
applied.replacement: A side-by-side look at the two best-known credit scoring brands and why the score on a free app may not match the one a lender pulls.
applied.why: SOURCE says two best-known brands, not main models.

applied.quote: Comes in multiple versions, and the version shown depends on the lender or free service displaying it
applied.why: SOURCE does not say how free services choose VantageScore versions.

applied.quote: Paying every bill on time and keeping balances low against your credit limits changes data that FICO and VantageScore both read.
applied.replacement: Bill-paying history and how much available credit you use are data that FICO and VantageScore both read.
applied.why: SOURCE lists factors only; does not give this behavioral advice.

applied.quote: The two usually move in the same direction, so a free VantageScore that climbs over several months suggests the FICO version the lender uses is climbing too.
applied.replacement: The two usually move in the same direction when your habits change.
applied.why: SOURCE says scores usually move together; months-long inference not stated.

applied.quote: The trend tells you more than any single reading.
applied.why: Comparative claim not stated in SOURCE.

applied.quote: You can get your scores for free through several legitimate channels, and our guide to [what a good credit score is](/guides/what-is-a-good-credit-score/) lists them.

applied.quote: At ModernWallet, we publish free calculators and plain-language money guides, and every credit guide we write starts from the score the lender will read.
applied.replacement: At ModernWallet, we publish plain-language money guides and free calculators.
applied.why: Practice claim about credit guides not licensed; keep minimal true company claim.

applied.quote: We do not quote a minimum credit history for either one.
applied.why: Narrates page omissions instead of informing reader.

applied.quote: We do not give a percentage weight for each factor on this page.
applied.why: Narrates page omissions instead of informing reader.

applied.quote: The useful point for a borrower is direction: a habit that improves these inputs usually lifts both scores together.
applied.replacement: A habit that improves these inputs usually lifts both scores together.

applied.quote: The two usually move in the same direction when your habits change. That signal is about direction only.
applied.replacement: The two usually move in the same direction when your habits change, but that signal shows direction only.

applied.quote: Our guide to the [credit score for a 0% annual percentage rate (APR) credit card](/guides/credit-score-for-0-apr-credit-card/) shows how that works for one card type.

applied.quote: Pull your credit reports this week, write down which model each free score uses, and ask your next lender which score it pulls.
applied.replacement: Pull your credit reports, write down which model each free score uses, and ask your next lender which score it pulls.

applied.quote: Because the scales match, a FICO number and a VantageScore number look interchangeable on a screen, even though separate formulas produced them.

applied.why: SOURCE never links secured cards to thin files or first cards.
